evidenceSummary.excerpt: For the rough Cyclops, who by Jove's command Temper'd the bolt and turn'd it to his hand, Work'd up less flame and fury in its make, And quench'd it sooner in the standing lake.
But, although so much milder than usual, this apparition was more than poor Semele's human nerves could bear, and she dropped to the floor in a swoon at the first glimpse of her lover.

Semele herself perished, burned to death; and the only person in all the building who escaped uninjured was Bacchus (Liber, Dionysus), the infant son of Jupiter and Semele, who was saved by his father's powerful hand.
